title: AI made games and mods playable?
author: LiquidThoughtsG
selftext:
I’ve seen mods, decomps, mashups and more all over my social media. When I look up some of these projects, as impressive as they are.. they aren’t in a playable state. Also when I say playable I mean I want a mostly bug free enjoyable experience. I’m just not an early access guy. I wait for the game to as perfect as possible so it does not break my immersion.

So my question is how far along is AI development. I understand that is really a project by project answer but in general can someone who has no experience build a fully finished game? The only finished stuff I’ve seen has been AI slop. What I mean is clearly half baked and messy.

There is a couple games/mashups/mods I’m dying to play but I want it to be a fully finished experience.

Escape from Duckov coop. There are mods but it’s really not very good yet.

Skyrim coop, Crimson Desert coop, Breath of the Wild coop. (Full quest, progression, items, ect synced)

I know this is a tall order but it seems like some insane progress is being made. Someone mad a big coop mode for BOTW with a lot of players. So it works but just no quests or progression. It’s basically just a sandbox.

So I guess my question is:  
Is there any projects that are actually finished and playable?  
Is there something I can use to fix existing mods?  
Is it far enough I can build something myself? If so what tools are suggested or tutorials?

comments.author: lemming1607
comments.body: Ai hasn't really changed anything that previous new tools did...the crap buggy games will always exist, and we will have to sort through them to find games that are well executed

comments.author: Fincut
comments.body:
I've noticed the same thing. So many impressive GIFs floating around, but when you actually check out the projects, there's barely a game behind them.

But yes, it's absolutely possible. I started with zero game dev experience and spent about 300 hours building a fully 3D Battleship game "Bearing Unknown", set in the Cold War. Four maps, different game modes, aircraft, helicopters, torpedoes, air defense, Steam multiplayer, the whole thing (try it for free: [https://wildstone-studios.com/](https://wildstone-studios.com/)

And it works. It's a finished game, not some fancy tech demo. I'm literally just waiting for Valve to approve my tax information so I can put it on Steam for a few bucks.

I still have no idea how to actually code, btw. I just know exactly what I want, and I'm pretty stubborn when something doesn't work.

Of course, making a Battleship game and getting Skyrim's entire quest system working in multiplayer are two VERY different things. I wouldn't even know where to start with the latter.
